highlights:
# Chrome Devtools Protocol - What does the scale parameter do in the clip argument?
...
I am trying to take the screenshot of an element selected by the user. To take the screenshot, I get the ClientBoundingRect for the element, add scrollX and scrollY to the x and y locations of the ClientBoundingRect and then set the x, y, height, width of the clip argument to the Page.captureScreenshot. There is another parameter to the clip argument called scale. I do not understand what the parameter does. Here are my observations:
...
If the set scale to 0, then the screenshot that gets captured is empty.
...
If I set the scale to 1, then the screenshot is non empty, is of the right size, but it captures the wrong part of the screen. I also notice that when the screenshot is being taken, the viewport size reduces to the height and width specified in clip parameter.
...
My questions are as follows:

What does the scale parameter do?
...
What would be the right way of capturing the screenshot of an element, selected by the user.
...
[1]https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Page/#method-captureScreenshot
...
[2]https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Page/#type-Viewport
...
**Vaibhav** (score: 0): I also noticed that the clip argument requires all the parameters in Device Independent Pixels instead of Pixels. Is there a conversion required?
